items.title: fix(query): validate media type tokens in requireContentType
items.body:
Resolves #1633

### Summary of Changes

- **Media Type Token Validation:** Per [RFC 9110 §8.3.1 and §5.6.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#name-media-type), a media type consists of `<type>/<subtype>` where `type` and `subtype` must each be a valid HTTP `token` (`1*tchar`).
  - Previously, `requireContentType` only verified `slash <= 0 || slash === mediaType.length - 1`, allowing malformed Content-Type values with multiple slashes (e.g. `application/json/extra`), whitespace (e.g. `application/json junk`), or delimiters (e.g. `application/(json)`) to erroneously match when wildcard acceptance (e.g. `application/*`) was used.
  - Replaced the simple slash index check with `MEDIA_TYPE_RE = /^[!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~0-9a-zA-Z]+\/[!#$%&'*+\-.^_`|~0-9a-zA-Z]+$/`, ensuring malformed media types consistently throw `422 Unprocessable Content` regardless of whether exact or wildcard matching is configured.
- **Tests:**
  - Added unit test in `test/query.test.ts` verifying that extra slashes, embedded whitespace, and invalid delimiter characters reject with 422 under wildcard acceptance.
  - All 3,120 tests pass across the entire suite.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **Bug Fixes**
  - Malformed `Content-Type` values are now rejected with a 422 response, including values with extra slashes, trailing characters, or invalid punctuation.

items.title: fix: return 412 for non-safe methods on matching If-None-Match
items.body:
Resolves #1623

### Summary of Changes

- **RFC 9110 §13.1.2 Compliance:** When evaluating conditional requests with `If-None-Match`:
  - For safe methods (`GET`, `HEAD`, and `QUERY` per RFC 10008), a matching entity tag resolves to `304 Not Modified`.
  - For other methods (such as `POST`, `PUT`, `DELETE`, `PATCH`), [RFC 9110 §13.1.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110#section-13.1.2) specifies that the recipient MUST NOT perform the requested method and SHOULD generate a `412 (Precondition Failed)` response. Previously, `handleCacheHeaders` unconditionally emitted `304`.
- **RFC 9110 §13.1.3 Compliance:** `If-Modified-Since` MUST be ignored if the request method is neither `GET` nor `HEAD` (or `QUERY`). For non-safe methods (like `POST`), `If-Modified-Since` without `If-None-Match` no longer halts execution or returns `304`/`412`.
- **RFC 9110 §13.2.1 Compliance:** Conditional headers are ignored for `OPTIONS`, `TRACE`, and `CONNECT`.
- **Tests:**
  - Added unit tests in `test/utils.test.ts` verifying `412` for `POST`/`PUT` with matching `If-None-Match`, `304` for `GET`, ignoring `If-Modified-Since` for `POST`, and ignoring conditional headers for `OPTIONS`.
  - All 3,118 tests pass across the repository.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Conditional cache requests now return the appropriate status for different request methods: matching validators return 304 for GET, HEAD, and QUERY, and 412 for other methods.
  * `If-Modified-Since` is applied only to GET, HEAD, and QUERY. Conditional cache headers are ignored for OPTIONS, TRACE, and CONNECT.
